searches.note: Twenty four searches of a share of twenty eight, four left unspent, none of them the author's. Five were restricted to one or two domains: disznoko.hu twice, disznoko.hu with its importer gonzalezbyass.com once and dobogo.hu once, read as primary through their summaries, and thedrinksbusiness.com once for the rules of March 2026. Ten kept domains out so that the second source would be independent: royal-tokaji.com five times, temposvegasicilia.com twice, dobogo.hu with its importer once, and a critic's own site four times, sometimes together. Nine went to the open web. The five shared searches are the vineyard classification of Tokaj, the Aszú rules of 2013, the eighteen months in barrel, the revised rules of March 2026 and the grape Zéta. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the facts a card or a question rests on (the first wine of 1990, the soak of the Oremus berries, the steeping at Disznókő, the dry Úrágya of 2000, the Zwack years), then to the sites and the makings, then to the rules of the appellation, with the house's own domain kept out wherever a second, independent source was wanted.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on the author's reading alone, it was cut or said with less (the northern edge of Tarcal, the dry dust, the twenty to thirty lots, the noble families, the prize winning architect, the steep south face and the road, Tállya, the Furmint alone of Mandulás).

Facts of a house's own history told on its own pages stand, hedged as the house's account; no person is named in prose; the dead met here (Péter Zwack, the preacher of the legend, the compiler of the survey of 1732) are described.

Sources whose title or address names a living person, or a writer's own site, were met among the results but are cited neither in the fragment nor here; the fragment's sources were left as the author wrote them, and the sources of this check are listed per change and per record under extraSources.

tested: Mézes Mály and Szarvas as the two vineyards above the first class: Grand Tokaj's vineyard page (the state's own estate, which holds Szarvas), Tokajneum and the Napa Valley Register agree on the two; the year is 1700, the 1730s or 1737 by account, so the record's eighteenth century stands with the doubt left open.

The vineyard's history: a Tarcal estate's page on its sites and a Hungarian review record the Mézesmál hill in 1280 and again in 1411, the modern plot at the western tip of the old hill; the record's sixteenth century and northern edge were found nowhere and are changed; a shop's page calls it a warm plot on loess, as the house does.

The founding of 1990, about sixty growers and the founders described, not named: Wine-Searcher, Waitrose and Decanter's first decade tasting agree; Berry Bros. and Rudd gives 1989. Confirmed as the library has it.

The first wine and the first decade: the house's page for its Betsek Aszú 5 Puttonyos of 1990 calls it the first historic vintage, and Decanter gives Aszú alone from 1990 to 1999 and grapes bought until 1993. Confirmed; the card now names the 5 Puttonyos.
The winery of 2010 for the twentieth year: Waitrose and one other account. Confirmed.

The making: two days in fermenting must stands on the house's 2018 sheet; the casks are of three hundred and five hundred litres, used, of Zemplén oak, for about two years, by Decanter on the 2019 Aszús, the importer's sheets for 2008 and 2016 and the house's word on its oak since 2010. Changed.
The cellars of the thirteenth century: two importer accounts repeat the house; one says they were dug against the Turks, which would make them later. Kept hedged, left open.

The label: Tokaji Aszú at 120 grams and 6 Puttonyos at 150, optional since the reform of 2013, by Wikipedia, Decanter and Wine Folly; the revised rules of March 2026 change no puttonyos figure that The Drinks Business reports. Confirmed.
The questions: four meanings and four years, one key each; 1992 is Disznókő's purchase and 1737 the royal decree. Sound.
The rules: nobody living named (the writer, the winemaker from Denmark and the merchant are described); no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The legend of about 1630 and the document of 1571: the study in Történelmi Szemle calls the legend unfounded and places the Oremus vineyard on the Várhegy at Sátoraljaújhely; Hello Hungary gives the Garai inventory of 1571 and says the preacher's great work of 1624 mentions no Aszú; wein.plus gives the vineyard. Confirmed, and the chronicle's line changed.

The purchase of 1993 and the winery of 1999 joined to cellars the house traces to the thirteenth century: Wine with Seth, Visit Tokaj and BOR 2025 give both years; the cellars are dated the twelfth, thirteenth or sixteenth century by account, so the hedge stays.

The making: three merchants' sheets of the house's Aszú 6 give six puttonyos of 25 kilograms to a gönci of 136 litres of must, fermentation in new Hungarian oak for one to two months, and two to three years in barrels of 136 and 220 litres; the soak is twelve to twenty four hours in one and a day or two in another, not two days. Changed.
The grapes: Furmint, Hárslevelű, Zéta and Sárga Muskotály across the sheets, with a share of Muscat in 2017. Confirmed.

The estate's vineyards: the region's listing of the estate names plots called Oremus, Mandulás, Petrács and Kútpatka; Berry Bros. and Rudd calls Petrács andesite. The sites now say volcanic rock and clay.
Zéta, once Oremus, a cross of Furmint and Bouvier, renamed in 1999: Wines of Hungary and the Tokaj tourism page, with a merchant who gives the estate's name as the reason. Confirmed.
The questions: four methods, one key; four years, one key. The key's soak is now a day or two. Sound once changed.
The rules: the preacher is described, the family of Vega Sicilia is named as a family, no living person named; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The history: the estate's history page gives the Vinea Disznókő of 1413, the survey of 1732 by János Matolai published in Mátyás Bél's Notitia, the purchase by AXA Millésimes in 1992, the replanting of 1994 at much higher density with better orientation and modern trellising, and its first class sites Disznókő, Hangács and Lajos. Confirmed as the estate's account; nothing on noble families or a state farm, only intensive cultivation before 1992.
The name: the estate's page on the origin of the name gives the large volcanic rock and the hill's shape. Confirmed.
The winery of 1995 by a Hungarian architect and the cellar about ten metres down in the rhyolite: the estate's facilities page. Confirmed; prize winning was in no source and is cut.

The making: the estate's sheets give most berries whole for about two days in fermenting must (about sixty hours in 2016), the rest crushed for about twelve hours, fermentation mostly in steel and partly in small barrels, and about two years in barrels of 225 litres with a little new oak, blended in January or March; the share of whole berries runs from about two fifths to two thirds. The twenty to thirty lots were not found, and two years and more becomes about two years.
The serve: the estate's sheet for 2017 advises 11 to 13 degrees Celsius; the record now gives it beside the Codex's 6 to 8.
The grapes: the González Byass sheet for 2016 gives the aszú berries as Furmint alone. Confirmed.
The questions: four ways of steeping, one key; four years, one key. The explanation's seven tenths becomes most. Sound once changed.
The rules: the architect and the compiler of the survey are described; no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The dry Úrágya of 2000: Falstaff tells of the head of the family's newly bought Úrágya vineyard taking no noble rot in 2000, the healthy grapes fermented dry, not the first dry Furmint of Tokaj but credited with setting off a movement; Decanter's piece on ageing Furmint places the wine of 2000 at Királyudvar, where he then worked; Decanter's review of the 2003 calls it the first dry Furmint under the family's label. The year stands; whose estate it was made for and the start of modern dry Tokaji are changed.
The family since the sixteenth century: two merchants' pages give the late sixteenth century or the 1500s. Confirmed, hedged as the family's account.

The communist years and 1990: two accounts have him delivering the grapes of his own vines to the state until 1990, a third has him running the state's wine plant at Mád; for 1990 he is the new company's manager in one, a founding investor and a driving force of Royal Tokaji in others. Changed: he took a leading part in founding it.

The site of Szent Tamás: two merchants' and a grower's pages give red clay over rhyolite tuff and zeolite; Royal Tokaji's own wine of the vineyard comes from a west facing flank and another grower's parcel faces south west; no source gave a south face or the road. Changed.
The first class rank of Szent Tamás: Royal Tokaji's labels and a grower's note. Kept, open.

The making: two merchants' sheets give fermentation in Hungarian oak barrels of three hundred litres, new and one year old, and three to eight months on the lees; native or added yeast differs between them. Changed, settling the author's open question.
A winery of Mád named Szent Tamás: En Primeur Club and the Tokaj wine knights' auction list it. The trap is changed.
The questions: four styles, one key; four years, one key, the stem now asking the movement and not another estate. Sound once changed.
The rules: the head of the family and his son are described; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The founding of 1995 in the centre of Tokaj town, by the Zwack family, the name from the hooves on the cobbles, and the partner of 2003: the house's own English and Hungarian pages and Tokaj Reneszánsz. Confirmed.

The plan's 1869: an importer's fact sheet dates the house to 1869 and another account calls it a house of 1869 over an old cellar; the house speaks of a cellar of a hundred and fifty years. Added, hedged, as the house's building, not the founding.
The vineyards: two merchants' pages list Szent Tamás, Betsek and Úrágya at Mád; Tállya was in no source of this check; Falstaff says Úrágya was never ranked for sweet wine. Changed.

The Zwack years: the factory of 1840 in Pest, the nationalisation of 1948 and the escape with the recipe, the return of 1988 and the firm won back in 1989 or 1992 by account, the founder's father dead in 2012: Wikipedia, We Love Budapest, Emerging Europe and Portfolio. Pest replaces Budapest and the early 1990s become as communism ended.
The eighteen months in barrel the wine question's explanation cites: Decanter and The Drinks Business on the rules revised in 2026. Confirmed.
The making on Mylitta, a kilo to the litre, a day's soak and the years in cask and bottle: not found outside the house and its importer in this check; kept as the house's account, open.
The questions: four ageing regimes, one key; four drinks, one key once the pálinka, which the Zwack firm also sells, gives way to a beer. Sound once changed.
The rules: the founder, her partner and her father are described; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.
